title: ~게 되다 [ge dweda] (End up, come to)
shortExplanation: Used to express that an action or situation resulted naturally or unintentionally.
longExplanation: '~게 되다' is used to indicate that an action or state 'came to be' as a result of certain circumstances, often without direct intention. It can refer to an unexpected outcome or something that happened gradually and naturally. It frequently translates as 'end up doing' or 'come to do' in English.

examples.sentence: 비가 오는데 우산을 안 가져와서 젖게 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Biga oneunde usaneul an gajyeowaseo jeotge doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: It was raining, and I didn't bring an umbrella, so I ended up getting wet.

examples.sentence: 공부를 많이 하지 않아서 시험에 떨어지게 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Gongbureul manhi haji anaseo siheome tteoreojige doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: I didn't study much, so I ended up failing the exam.

examples.sentence: 저는 한국어를 많이 연습해서 한국어를 유창하게 말하게 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun hangukeoreul manhi yeonseubhaeseo hangukeoreul yuchanghage malhage doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: I practiced Korean a lot, so I ended up speaking it fluently.

examples.sentence: 주말에 친구들과 만나려 했는데, 그들이 바빠서 결국 혼자 영화를 보게 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Jumare chingudeulgwa mannalyeo haenneunde, geudeuri bappaseo gyeolguk honja yeonghwareul boge doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: I planned to meet my friends over the weekend, but they were busy, so I ended up watching a movie alone.

title: ~게 하다 [ge hada] (Make/cause someone to do)
shortExplanation: Used to express 'making' or 'causing' someone to do something.
longExplanation: '~게 하다' indicates that someone or something makes or causes another person to perform an action. It corresponds to 'make/let/cause (someone) do something' in English. The subject is the person causing the action, and the object is the one who is made to do it.

examples.sentence: 어머니는 동생 명주를 공부하게 하셨어요, 그래서 명주는 시험을 잘 볼 수 있었습니다.
examples.romanization: Eomeonineun dongsaeng Myeongjureul gongbuhage hasyeosseoyo, geuraeseo Myeongjuneun siheomeul jal bol su isseotseumnida.
examples.translation: Mother made my younger sibling Myeongju study, so Myeongju was able to do well on the exam.

examples.sentence: 사장님은 직원들을 일찍 회사에 도착하게 했습니다, 그래서 모든 사람이 일찍 일을 시작하게 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Sajangnimeun jigweondeureul iljjik hoesa-e dochakhage haesseumnida, geuraeseo modeun sarami iljjik ireul sijakhage doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: The boss made the employees arrive at the office early, so everyone started work early.

examples.sentence: 선생님은 학생들이 한국어 문장을 만들게 했어요, 그래서 학생들은 더 잘 이해하게 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Seonsaengnimeun haksaengdeuri hangugeo munjangeul mandeulge haesseoyo, geuraeseo haksaengdeureun deo jal ihaehage doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: The teacher made the students create Korean sentences, and they came to understand Korean better.

examples.sentence: 그 영화는 나를 웃게 했어요, 코미디 부분이 정말 재미있었거든요.
examples.romanization: Geu yeonghwaneun nareul utge haesseoyo, komidi bubuni jeongmal jaemiisseotgeodeunyo.
examples.translation: That movie made me laugh; its comedy parts were really entertaining.

title: ~고 말다 [go malda] (End up)
shortExplanation: Used to express that an action is completed or ends with an unexpected or unintended result.
longExplanation: '~고 말다' emphasizes that an action/event reached its conclusion (often regretfully or unexpectedly). It can carry the nuance of something happening despite efforts or intentions to avoid it, leading to a sense of finality or mild lament.

examples.sentence: 저는 연습을 너무 많이 해서 손가락이 아파 결국 연습을 멈추고 말았어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun yeonseubeul neomu mani haeseo songaragi apa gyeolguk yeonseubeul meomchugo malasseoyo.
examples.translation: I practiced too much, so my fingers hurt and I ended up stopping practice.

examples.sentence: 친구가 계속 추천해서 결국 그 영화를 보고 말았어요, 그런데 별로 재미없었어요.
examples.romanization: Chinguga gyesok chucheonhaeseo gyeolguk geu yeonghwareul bogo malasseoyo, geureonde byeollo jaemieopseosseoyo.
examples.translation: My friend kept recommending it, so I finally ended up watching that movie, but it wasn’t very good.

examples.sentence: 너무 배가 고파서 그녀가 만든 요리를 다 먹고 말았습니다, 사실 재료 선택이 조금 별로였어요.
examples.romanization: Neomu baega gopaseo geunyeoga mandeun yorireul da meokgo malasseumnida, sasil jaeryo seontaegi jogeum byeolloyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: I was so hungry that I ended up eating all the food she made; honestly, the ingredient choices weren’t great.

examples.sentence: 하루 종일 일하고 너무 피곤해서 잠들고 말았어요, 그래서 계획했던 일을 다 못 했습니다.
examples.romanization: Haru jongil ilhago neomu pigonhaeseo jamdeulgo malasseoyo, geuraeseo gyehoekhaetdeon ireul da mot haesseumnida.
examples.translation: After working all day I was so tired that I ended up falling asleep, so I couldn’t finish my planned tasks.

title: ~고 말하다 [go malhada] (Say that...)
shortExplanation: Used to convey that someone said something in a manner suggesting finality or firm intention.
longExplanation: The construction '~고 말하다' in Korean means 'to say (something).' It can carry a nuance of definitiveness or insistence in the statement. It is often used when someone states a fact, an order, or a firm decision they have made.

examples.sentence: 그녀는 배가 불러도 작은 케이크 한 조각을 더 먹겠다고 말했어요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoneun baega bulleodo jageun keikeu han jogageul deo meokgetdago malhaesseoyo.
examples.translation: She said that she would eat another slice of cake even though she was already full.

examples.sentence: 우리 어머니는 저녁에 일찍 잘 것이라고 말했어요. 너무 피곤해서 그렇대요.
examples.romanization: Uri eomeonineun jeonyeoge iljjik jal geosirago malhaesseoyo. Neomu pigonhaeseo geureotaeyo.
examples.translation: My mother said she would go to bed early tonight. She said it’s because she’s very tired.

examples.sentence: 회사 대표는 상황이 어렵다고 말했습니다, 그래서 직원들은 더 집중해야겠다고 느꼈어요.
examples.romanization: Hoesa daepyeoneun sanghwangi eoryeopdago malhaesseumnida, geuraeseo jigweondeureun deo jipjunghaeyagetdago neukkyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: The company’s CEO said that things are difficult, so the employees felt they should focus more.

examples.sentence: 그는 결코 포기하지 않겠다고 말해서, 모두가 그의 결심을 믿게 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun gyeolko pogihaji angetdago malhaeseo, moduga geuui gyeolsimeul mitge doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: He said he would never give up, so everyone came to trust his determination.

title: ~고 보면 [go bomyeon] (Upon closer look, when you consider)
shortExplanation: Used to express the meaning 'when seen/considered in a certain way' or 'once you look at it, you realize...'.
longExplanation: '~고 보면 [go bomyeon]' conveys the idea that after doing or seeing something, a new perspective or outcome emerges. It indicates that things may look different 'when you actually do/see them'.

examples.sentence: 처음에는 문제가 어려워 보였지만, 자세히 보고 보면 그렇게 어렵지 않아요.
examples.romanization: Cheoeumeneun munjega eoryeowo boyeotjiman, jasehi bogo bomyeon geureoke eoryeopji anhayo.
examples.translation: At first the problem looked difficult, but when you examine it closely, it's not that hard.

examples.sentence: 그의 아이디어가 처음에는 이상하게 들렸지만, 곰곰이 생각해 보고 보면 굉장히 독창적이에요.
examples.romanization: Geuui aideoga cheoeumeneun isanghage deullyeotjiman, gomgomi saenggakae bogo bomyeon goaengjanghi dokchangjeogiyeyo.
examples.translation: His idea sounded strange at first, but when you think it over, it's actually very innovative.

examples.sentence: 사진을 보고 보면 그가 꽤 행복해 보이네요.
examples.romanization: Sajineul bogo bomyeon geuga kkwae haengbokhae boineyo.
examples.translation: When I look at the photo, he actually seems quite happy.

examples.sentence: 이 책을 읽고 보면 작가의 의도를 더 잘 이해할 수 있을 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: I chaegeul ilkgo bomyeon jakgaui uidoeul deo jal ihaehal su isseul geot gatayo.
examples.translation: Once you read this book, I think you'll understand the author’s intention much better.

title: ~고서 [goseo] (After doing)
shortExplanation: Used to express that an action is performed after the execution of another action.
longExplanation: '~고서 [goseo]' is a Korean grammar form used to indicate that another action or event occurs after the first action has been completed. It roughly translates to 'after doing something.' This construction usually implies that the same subject completes one action and then proceeds somewhat directly to the next.

examples.sentence: 지난 주에 도서관에 갔어요. 책을 빌리고서 돌아왔어요.
examples.romanization: Jinan ju-e doseogwan-e gasseoyo. Chaegeul bil-ri-go-seo dorawasseoyo.
examples.translation: I went to the library last week and came back after borrowing a book.

examples.sentence: 집에 도착하자마자 밥을 먹고서 씻었어요.
examples.romanization: Jibe dochakha-jamaja babeul meok-go-seo ssiseosseoyo.
examples.translation: As soon as I arrived home, I ate and then washed up.

examples.sentence: 나는 숙제를 다 하고서 TV를 봤어요.
examples.romanization: Naneun sugjereul da ha-go-seo tibireul bwasseoyo.
examples.translation: I watched TV after finishing all my homework.

examples.sentence: 우리는 수영장에서 수영을 하고서 밥을 먹었어요.
examples.romanization: Urineun suyeongjang-eseo suyeongeul ha-go-seo bab-eul meogeosseoyo.
examples.translation: We ate after swimming at the pool.

title: ~고자 [goja] (In order to)
shortExplanation: Used to express the purpose or aim of an action: 'in order to', 'for the purpose of'.
longExplanation: '~고자 [goja]' is used to express someone’s intention or goal—like 'in order to' in English. It clarifies the purpose of an action. Note that this form is somewhat formal or literary; in more casual speech, you might see different expressions such as '~려고'.

examples.sentence: 저는 토픽 시험을 통과하기 위해 한국어를 공부하고자 합니다.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun TOPIK siheomeul tong-gwa-hagi wihae hangukeoreul gongbuhagoja hamnida.
examples.translation: In order to pass the TOPIK exam, I intend to study Korean.

examples.sentence: 그녀는 자기 스스로를 향상시키고자 매일 운동을 합니다.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoneun jagi seuseuroreul hyangsang-sikigoja maeil undongeul hamnida.
examples.translation: She exercises daily in order to improve herself.

examples.sentence: 우리 아버지는 우리 가족을 위해 매일 일하고자 합니다.
examples.romanization: Uri abeojineun uri gajogeul wihae maeil ilhagoja hamnida.
examples.translation: My father intends to work every day in order to provide for our family.

examples.sentence: 우리는 환경을 보호하고자 재활용품을 구입하기로 결정했습니다.
examples.romanization: Urineun hwangyeongeul bohohagoja jaehwallyongpumeul guibhagiro gyeoljeonghaesseumnida.
examples.translation: In order to protect the environment, we decided to purchase recycled products.

title: ~기는 하다 [gineun hada] (Do something but...)
shortExplanation: Used to express 'I do (action) but...', showing a contrast with an additional clause.
longExplanation: '~기는 하다 [gineun hada]' acknowledges that something is true while introducing a contrasting or qualifying statement. The nuance is similar to 'I do X, but...' or 'Yes, it’s true that X, but...' in English.

examples.sentence: 저는 먹기는 했지만 그렇게 많이 먹지는 않았어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun meok-gineun haessjiman geureoke mani meokjineun anhasseoyo.
examples.translation: I did eat, but I didn't eat that much.

examples.sentence: 제가 그 영화를 보기는 했는데 재미있게는 보지 못했어요.
examples.romanization: Jega geu yeonghwareul bo-gineun haenneunde jaemiitge-neun boji moshaesseoyo.
examples.translation: I did watch that movie, but I didn't really find it fun.

examples.sentence: 그는 운동을 하기는 한다. 그러나 건강한 식생활은 유지하지 않아요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun undongeul ha-gineun handa. Geureona geonganghan siksaenghwareun yuji haji anhayo.
examples.translation: He does exercise, but he doesn't maintain a healthy diet.

examples.sentence: 나는 한국어를 배우기는 하지만 아직은 잘 못해요.
examples.romanization: Naneun hangukeoreul baeugineun hajiman ajigeun jal motaeyo.
examples.translation: I do study Korean, but I still can't speak it well.

title: ~기로 하다 [giro hada] (Decide to)
shortExplanation: Used to express the decision or resolution to do something.
longExplanation: '~기로 하다 [giro hada]' is used to indicate that someone has decided or resolved to carry out a particular action. It can refer to personal decisions or collectively agreed plans, often used when describing future intentions.

examples.sentence: 나는 매일 아침 운동하기로 결정했어요, 그래서 날씨가 춥더라도 매일 운동하고 있어요.
examples.romanization: Naneun maeil achim undonghagiro gyeoljeonghaesseoyo, geuraeseo nalssiga chupdeorado maeil undonghago isseoyo.
examples.translation: I decided to exercise every morning, so I do it daily even if it's cold.

examples.sentence: 우리 모두 내년에 함께 여행 가기로 했어요, 그래서 지금부터 돈을 모으기로 했어요.
examples.romanization: Uri modu naenyeone hamkke yeohaeng gagiro haesseoyo, geuraeseo jigeumbuteo doneul moeugiro haesseoyo.
examples.translation: We all decided to travel together next year, so we've decided to start saving money now.

examples.sentence: 그는 올해 안에 흡연을 끊기로 했어요, 그래서 담배를 더 이상 사지 않기로 했어요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun olhae ane heubyeoneul kkeungiro haesseoyo, geuraeseo dambaereul deo isang saji anhgiro haesseoyo.
examples.translation: He decided to quit smoking this year, so he decided not to buy cigarettes anymore.

examples.sentence: 회사는 직원들의 안전을 위해 매주 금요일에 마스크를 착용하기로 했어요.
examples.romanization: Hoesaneun jigweondeur-ui anjeoneul wihae maeju geumyoire maseukeureul chakyonghagiro haesseoyo.
examples.translation: The company decided to wear masks every Friday for the employees’ safety.

title: ~기로 되다 [giro dweda] (It is decided/settled)
shortExplanation: Used to express that something has been officially decided or settled.
longExplanation: '~기로 되다 [giro dweda]' is used when a decision has been made—often collectively or officially—and is now settled. It is akin to ‘It has been decided that...’ in English.

examples.sentence: 우리는 다음 주에 여행 가기로 되었어요. 날짜는 이미 정해졌어요.
examples.romanization: Urineun daeum ju-e yeohaeng gagiro doeeosseoyo. Naljja-neun imi jeonghaejyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: It's been decided that we'll travel next week. The date has already been set.

examples.sentence: 그녀는 자세한 계획을 세우기로 되었어요. 다음 달에 결혼식을 준비 중이에요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoneun jasehan gyehoekeul seugiro doeeosseoyo. Daeum dale gyeolhonsigeul junbi jungieyo.
examples.translation: It was settled that she would make a detailed plan. She’s preparing for a wedding next month.

examples.sentence: 우리는 매주 목요일마다 회의를 하기로 되었어요, 모든 팀원이 참석할 수 있는 시간이에요.
examples.romanization: Urineun maeju mogyoil-mada hoeuireul hagiro doeeosseoyo, modeun timweon-i chamseokhal su itneun siganieyo.
examples.translation: It has been decided that we’ll hold meetings every Thursday, as that’s a time everyone can attend.

examples.sentence: 누구를 팀 리더로 선발할지는 이미 결정되었고, 그가 그 역할을 맡기로 되었어요.
examples.romanization: Nugureul tim lideoro seonbalhaljineun imi gyeoljeongdoeeotgo, geuga geu yeokhareul matgiro doeeosseoyo.
examples.translation: Who would be chosen as the team leader was already decided, and he was settled to take on that role.

title: ~기 시작하다 [gi sijak-hada] (Begin to)
shortExplanation: Used to express the beginning of an action or state.
longExplanation: '~기 시작하다 [gi sijak-hada]' means 'to start doing something.' It's comparable to 'begin to' or 'start to' in English. It emphasizes that an action or condition has just begun.

examples.sentence: 저는 한국어를 배우기 시작하려고 이 학교에 왔어요. 전에는 전혀 몰랐어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun hangukeoreul baeugi sijak-haryeogo i hakgyoe wasseoyo. Jeoneneun jeonhyeo mollasseoyo.
examples.translation: I came to this school to start learning Korean. I knew nothing before.

examples.sentence: 운동을 본격적으로 시작하려고 헬스클럽에 등록했어요. 건강에 좋다고 하더라고요.
examples.romanization: Undongeul bongyeokjeogeuro sijak-haryeogo helseu-keulleobe deungnokhaesseoyo. Geongange johdago hadeoragoyo.
examples.translation: I registered at the gym to start exercising seriously. They say it’s good for your health.

examples.sentence: 요즘 아침에 일어나기 시작하면 커피를 꼭 한 잔 마셔요.
examples.romanization: Yojeum achim-e il-eonagi sijak-hamyeon keopireul kkok han jan masyeoyo.
examples.translation: These days, whenever I start my morning, I definitely have a cup of coffee.

examples.sentence: 그날 이후로는 매일 영화를 보기 시작했어요. 사람들의 다양한 이야기를 접하고 싶거든요.
examples.romanization: Geu-nal ihuroneun maeil yeonghwareul bogi sijak-haesseoyo. Saramdeurui dayanghan iyagireul jeophago sipgeodeunyo.
examples.translation: Since that day, I started watching movies every day because I want to encounter various people's stories.

title: ~기 전에 [gi jeone] (Before)
shortExplanation: '~기 전에' is used to express 'before doing something'.
longExplanation: '~기 전에 [gi jeone]' means 'before (doing something).' It marks that one action or state happens prior to another. Commonly used with the infinitive form of the verb plus '기 전에'.

examples.sentence: 여행을 가기 전에 짐을 싸야 돼요.
examples.romanization: Yeohaengeul gagi jeone jimeul ssaya dwaeyo.
examples.translation: You need to pack your luggage before going on a trip.

examples.sentence: 미팅 시작하기 전에 발표 준비를 마쳤어요.
examples.romanization: Miting sijak-hagi jeone balpyo junbireul machyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: I finished preparing my presentation before the meeting started.

examples.sentence: 저는 항상 운동하기 전에 스트레칭을 합니다.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun hangsang undong-hagi jeone seuteurechingeul hamnida.
examples.translation: I always stretch before I exercise.

examples.sentence: 시험 보기 전에 충분히 공부했어요.
examples.romanization: Siheom bogi jeone chungbunhi gongbuhaesseoyo.
examples.translation: I studied enough before taking the exam.

title: ~기 힘들다 [gi himdeulda] (It's hard to...)
shortExplanation: Expresses difficulty in performing an action or task.
longExplanation: '~기 힘들다 [gi himdeulda]' is used to describe that it's difficult or hard to do something. '힘들다' means 'hard' or 'tough,' while the preceding '~기' nominalizes the verb, turning it into 'doing X is hard.'

examples.sentence: 매일 아침 일찍 일어나기 힘들어요, 하지만 어쩔 수 없어요.
examples.romanization: Maeil achim iljjik ireonagi himdeureoyo, hajiman eojjeol su eopseoyo.
examples.translation: It's hard to wake up early every morning, but I have no choice.

examples.sentence: 한국어를 배우는 게 처음에는 어려웠지만, 계속 연습해도 익숙해지기 힘들다는 걸 깨달았어요.
examples.romanization: Hangukeoreul baeuneun ge cheoeumeneun eoryeowotjiman, gyesok yeonseuphaedo iksukhaejigi himdeuldaneun geol kkaedaratseoyo.
examples.translation: At first, learning Korean was tough, but I realized it's still hard to get used to it even with continued practice.

examples.sentence: 매일 운동하기 힘들지만, 건강을 위해 꾸준히 하려고 해요.
examples.romanization: Maeil undong-hagi himdeuljiman, geongangeul wihae kkujunhi haryeogo haeyo.
examples.translation: It's hard to exercise every day, but I'm trying to do it consistently for my health.

examples.sentence: 사람들 앞에서 말하기가 정말 힘들어요, 아직도 계속 연습 중이에요.
examples.romanization: Saramdeul apeseo malhagiga jeongmal himdeureoyo, ajikdo gyesok yeonseup jungieyo.
examples.translation: It's really hard to speak in front of people; I'm still practicing.

title: ~기를 [gireul] (In order to)
shortExplanation: Used to indicate the purpose or motive behind an action, similar to 'in order to'.
longExplanation: '~기를 [gireul]' is attached to a verb (in its nominalized form) to mean 'in order to do X' or 'for the purpose of doing X.' It's frequently followed by expressions like '위해(서)' (wihae[seo]), highlighting intent or purpose.

examples.sentence: 이 해외 여행은 영어를 배우기를 위해 가는 거예요.
examples.romanization: I haeoe yeohaengeun yeongeoreul baeugireul wihae ganeun geoyeyo.
examples.translation: I'm going on this overseas trip in order to learn English.

examples.sentence: 아침 일찍 일어났어요, 강의를 듣기를 위해서요.
examples.romanization: Achim iljjik ireonasseoyo, ganguireul deudgireul wihaeseoyo.
examples.translation: I woke up early in order to attend the lecture.

examples.sentence: 그는 집을 사기를 위해 돈을 모았어요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun jibeul sagireul wihae doneul moasseoyo.
examples.translation: He saved money in order to buy a house.

examples.sentence: 그녀는 책을 쓰기를 위해 많은 경험을 쌓았어요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoneun chaegeul sseugireul wihae manheun gyeongheomeul ssahasseoyo.
examples.translation: She accumulated a lot of experience in order to write a book.

title: ~기만 하다 [giman hada] (Just)
shortExplanation: '~기만 하다' is used to express that someone or something does only the mentioned action and nothing else.
longExplanation: The grammar point '~기만 하다' is used in Korean to show exclusivity of action — that the verb in question is the only thing done. The nominalized form (~기) plus '만 하다' implies 'only do X.' Often, it can carry a slightly negative nuance or express dissatisfaction because it implies that the action is insufficient or not meeting expectations.

examples.sentence: 나는 밤새 공부하기만 했어요, 다른 것은 하나도 하지 않았어요.
examples.romanization: Naneun bamsae gongbu-hagiman haesseoyo, dareun geoseun hanado haji anhasseoyo.
examples.translation: I just studied all night and didn't do anything else.

examples.sentence: 우리 아버지는 텔레비전을 보기만 해서 그게 걱정이에요.
examples.romanization: Uri abeojineun tellebijeoneul bogiman haeseo geuge geokjeong-ieyo.
examples.translation: My father only watches television, which worries me.

examples.sentence: 그는 매일 같은 식당에 가서 먹기만 해요. 건강에 좋지 않아요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun maeil gateun sikdang-e gaseo meok-giman haeyo. Geongange joji anhayo.
examples.translation: He just goes to the same restaurant every day to eat. It's not healthy.

examples.sentence: 우리 친구는 게임하기만 하면서 시간을 허비해요.
examples.romanization: Uri chinguneun geim-hagiman hamyeonseo siganeul heobihaeyo.
examples.translation: Our friend only plays games and wastes time.
